speaker: Nyssa
text: The sporekin have eaten another tray of moonpetal shoots. Lovely creatures. Terrible neighbours.

speaker: Nyssa
text: Dewdrop spriggles and glasspond frogs like the lower shade. Higher up you will find lantern imps, petalguards and walking saplings. Give the petal drakes their space.

speaker: Pip
text: If you smell something sweet, that is supper. If you smell burnt sugar, I was talking too much.

speaker: Pip
text: The cooking pot is on the market counter. Bring your own ingredients. There is a crafting bench here too, and the furnace and anvil are by the forge.

speaker: Tansy
text: Dewglass looks soft under this light. It still needs a proper furnace. I have a ruined hammer to prove it.

speaker: Tansy
text: Take the eastern lane to Dewglass Workings. Lantern Seam is farther into the garden. Bank your load here before heading out again.

speaker: Wren
text: I have walked to Prism Hollow twice today. The harts keep stopping in the path to stare at me.

options.text: How do I reach Prism Hollow?

speaker: Wren
text: Follow the paths through Moonpath Cross and keep north. The threshold leads straight into the deeper garden. Its creatures are stronger, so stop at the bank before you explore.

speaker: Ione
text: The orchid pondlings hide under these leaves. I water the flowers around them. Moving a frog is more work than moving a watering can.

options.text: What is different about these gardens?

speaker: Ione
text: Starcap snails graze in the hollows while the porcelain reliquaries patrol. Twilight imps gather above them. The deeper crowns belong to starroot tenders, orchid drakes and mineral wardlings.

speaker: Aster
text: Those lights overhead are not the surface stars. I keep drawing them anyway. Last week one of the patterns moved.

speaker: Aster
text: Great wardens settle on the high crowns. They carry the same old guardian jewels found elsewhere, though the garden has coloured their wings. Watch them from the approach before stepping into the clearing.

speaker: Thimble
text: Another cloak caught on a root. Bring it here before you decide the missing piece makes it fashionable.

options.text: Any advice for the high gardens?

speaker: Thimble
text: Use the narrow climbing paths. Some crowns have Agility climbs too, if you have the training. Leave yourself room to get back down; a drake can turn faster than you expect.

speaker: Serein
text: Star amethyst, yew, one muddy boot. People write unusual things in the gathering ledger.

speaker: Serein
text: Star Amethyst Cut lies west of the village. Orchid Yew Grove is east, and Starroot Garden is farther north. The bank here saves you the trip back to Lantern Rest.

speaker: Luma
text: Welcome to Lantern Rest. The bank is here in the village. Follow the lit paths when you leave; the high gardens have only a few ways up.

options.text: How do I reach the high gardens?

speaker: Luma
text: Look for a narrow path climbing around the rock. Most of those banks are too steep to walk up. The wider clearings farther from town are creature territory.

speaker: Brindle
text: Mind the roots beside the steps. We build into these banks because they shelter the cottages. Took years to get the moss back after the last roof went up.

options.text: Are the gardens outside town safe?
I will keep to the path.

speaker: Brindle
text: Safe enough here. Farther out, something always wants the same patch of shade you do. Leave room to retreat before you climb into an occupied clearing.

speaker: Vesper
text: This is Prism Hollow. Beyond it, Faeholme grows colder and the creatures grow stronger. Check the clearing above you before you take its climbing path.

speaker: Vesper
text: The largest strangers wander into every region. They are much stronger than the usual creatures, and their resting places can change. An empty path today proves very little about tomorrow.

options.text: I will look before I climb.

speaker: Rime
text: A good jewel earns its setting. Some protect the wearer; some lend strength to a blade or spell. The unusual ones can do both.

options.text: Where do the unusual jewels come from?
I will keep an eye out.

speaker: Rime
text: The roaming great monsters sometimes carry them. Ordinary jewelry is much more common. A rare piece can hold defense, health and strength together; those are the ones I record carefully.
Warden Ilse, Millfield, acting under Trade Company charter clause fourteen. You are welcome here, you are counted, and you are responsible for your own equipment. What do you need?

variants.text: The Carter has told me his version of your run. I have written down the version that matches the distances. Both are on file. What do you need?

options.text: Who in this town has work?
Is there a faster way to the pit than the road?

requires.reason: Warden Ilse only reads the charter to people who have settled a wager under it.

text: Four people. Harrow the Smith, east side of the square, will not sell you a weapon until you have made one. Pitmaster Dorn, by the bank counter, has a ledger problem he calls a pit problem. Ranger Syb, by the Rope House on the north-west side of the square, knows every useful water source in the region. Carter Bel is at the south gate and is wrong.

Two hundred and six people, one vault, one pit, and a road the Company built and then stopped maintaining. We keep the walls up. We keep the count. The Company has not answered a letter in nine years, and I have sent one every quarter, so the file is thorough if nothing else.

The Farm Road runs to the North Gate and into Woodlands. The trees there were surveyed as terrain rather than as trees, which tells you what the surveyor thought of them. Beyond Woodlands is Highlands. I have never been. It is not in my charter.

There are two. The Brook Planks cross Iron Brook at roughly minus seventy-eight, minus thirty, and save sixty-six metres on the trip to River Shallows. The Wall Vault goes over our own north wall and saves forty-four metres to the pit. Regulation nine forbids the second one. Nobody has obeyed regulation nine since it was written.

Clause fourteen. Any person within the wall is counted, is owed the wall's protection, and is owed an accurate record of what they are owed. That is the entire clause. It has outlived the company that wrote it, which I find I do not mind.
Metal costs. Skill does not. Which are you short of?

variants.text: Still on the dagger. Come back when it is done.
You made one. Now you can buy one.

options.text: How is the dagger meant to go?

requires.reason: Harrow will not hear about the dagger until you have made it and used it.
Harrow will not sell Cobalt work below Smithing 10. He says it would be a waste of the bar.

text: No. Make one first. Six Copper out of the Copper Pit. Two bars at my furnace. A dagger at my anvil. Then put it in something and tell me it held.

options.text: Fine. Six ore, two bars, a dagger.

text: Good. Pit is north, one hundred and sixty metres. Take the east gate. Frogs on the shallows when you are ready to test it, around minus fifty-six, minus seventy-two.
Ore, bar, dagger, use it. In that order. I do not explain twice.

variants.text: You have the ore. Furnace is by the anvil. Two bars.
Bars are made. Anvil next. A dagger, not a sword. You are not ready for a sword.
Wear it. Then find three frogs. Carrying a blade is not owning one.
Then say so.

text: Then it held. Take the hatchet, take the food, take the gold. You know how the whole trade works now. Everything after this is a bigger fire.
Copper here. Iron in Woodlands, green in the break. Cobalt on the moor, blue-black, splits with a line like lightning. Same three steps every time. Ore, bar, thing.
Cobalt dagger. Cobalt sword. Cobalt plate if you have the bars. Stall is behind me.
Four. Four loads a seam, that is what the ledger says, four, and I have signed it nine hundred and, no, nine hundred and forty-one times. Four. Have you ever seen a seam give four?

variants.text: Eleven point four average across the last six. Eleven point four! And the ledger said four. Nine years. Do not tell the Warden how long it took me.
Well? What did it give? Not four. It never gives four.

options.text: How many does a seam give?
I worked a seam to the bottom. Here is the count.

requires.reason: Dorn wants a number from a seam you personally emptied. Work one out first.

options.text: The vault holds fifteen. Sign the page.

requires.reason: The bank has to agree with the ledger first. Fifteen Copper ore in the Millfield vault.

options.text: Tell me about the Copper Pit.

text: Nobody knows! That is the, that is exactly the problem. Go up to the Copper Pit, pick one seam, and stay on it until it is finished. Not until you are bored. Until it is empty and it tells you so. Then come back with the number.

options.text: One seam, all the way down. Fine.
I have counting of my own to do.

text: One seam. One. If you swap nodes halfway the number is worthless and I will know, because the number will be wrong, and I will know it is wrong, because I know what wrong looks like, I have signed it nine hundred and forty-one times.
Go on then. Which band? And be honest, I would rather a true four than a flattering twelve. I would not, actually, but say it anyway.

options.text: Let me check my count again.

text: No. No, that is, that does not match anything, and I need it to match something. Go back up. Work another seam down to nothing and read what it gives you when it gives out. The pit will not mind. The pit has never minded.

That. That is a real number. Say it again while I write it. Nine years of four. Right, one more thing and it is finished: put fifteen Copper ore in the Millfield vault, so the store agrees with the page. A number nobody can weigh is a rumour.
Signed. Ledger, vault and pit, all three saying the same thing on the same day. Take the pickaxe, it is a good one, and take this before I count it again and change my mind.

Six Copper seams and two stone faces at the Copper Pit, one hundred and sixty metres due north. A seam comes back about twenty-one seconds after it empties, so if you work them in a ring the first is ready before the last runs out. That much I do know.
Wind off the moor, cold, steady, been like it for eleven weeks. The shallows are running clear enough to fish. That is the useful part.

options.text: Where is the water around here?
What is out on open meadow?

text: Three places worth a line. River Shallows here, minnow, shallow and red-silted. Blackwater Pools in Woodlands, trout, deeper than they look and colder than they look. Mountain Lakes on the moor, perch, and a second pair at the Far Lake across the gap.

Frogs in the wet ground by the shallows, minus fifty-six, minus seventy-two. They will not start it. Billy goats on the rise at Open Meadow, minus two-fifty, thirty. They will. Neither will kill you if you have eaten. That is most of what I know and all of what matters.

You! Settle something! The Warden says the pit road is the fast way. The Warden! Who has walked it, what, twice? Three times? I have walked it four thousand times and I am telling you the road is a lie the road tells about itself!

variants.text: There you are. Honest one. Cost me two weeks of cart duty and I would do it again, because now when I say a thing about a distance, people check, and I am right.
Ha! Best time on record! Unbeatable! Nobody has beaten it! Nobody has attempted it! Do not attempt it.
Are you running it or are you standing here? Those are different activities!

options.text: I ran it. Here is my time.

requires.reason: Bel wants both obstacles run: the Brook Planks first, then the Wall Vault.

text: Two weeks of cart duty, that is the bet! She says road. I say over. Over the Brook Planks at the brook, and over our own north wall at the Wall Vault. You cannot do the wall cold, mind, you have to have some legs on you first. Vault the planks until you are quick at it. Then the wall. Then come and tell me a number!

options.text: Planks, then wall. I will bring you a number.
I am on the Warden's side.

text: The Warden's side! Everyone is on the Warden's side! That is not the same as being right!

options.text: All right, tell me the bet again.

text: That is the spirit! The planks are at minus seventy-eight, minus thirty, anyone can do those, my aunt could do those. The wall wants some Agility in you, three of it, which is what the planks are for! Go! Go and be quick and come back slow so I can see your face!
Numbers! Give me numbers! And keep your voice up, the Warden is standing right there and I want this on the record.

options.text: Honestly? The wall saves about forty metres. Useful, not miraculous.
Call it a hundred metres saved. Round numbers travel better.
I did it in four seconds and landed on the roof of the vault.

text: There! You heard it! Cart duty! Two weeks! Take your cut, you have earned it, and if anyone asks, it was further than that.

variants.text: Forty. Forty metres. That is, hm. That is still faster, is it not? That is still faster. Warden! It is still faster! Take your cut. You could have lied and you did not, and I find I mind that less than I expected.
The roof! Of the vault! Did you hear that, Warden? ... She is writing it down. She is writing all of it down. Take your cut and go, go now, and do not come back through the square this week.

text: My cousin walked from here to Oakwood in a morning! A morning! Now, people say that is not possible, and to those people I say: he had a very good morning.
Stand a moment. The stand does not like a fast walker. ... There. Now. You are a miner, or a cutter. Cutter. I can tell by the shoulders. What do you want from my trees?

variants.text: Cutter. You went and looked at the split one. Not many do. Most take the eight and go home and never ask what the ninth was for.
Eight. Not nine. And you have somewhere to be first.

requires.reason: Ansel will not put a Ash in front of anyone under Woodcutting 5. He says the tree deserves better.

options.text: Eight Ash logs, and I went and saw the split one.

requires.reason: Fell the eight first, then go and stand at the Split Ash east of the pools.
You need 8 Ash logs in your bag. Logs do not stack, so that is 8 slots.

text: Eight. You may have eight. Ash Grove, north-west of Oakwood, ten trees there and eight is what the stand can spare this season. ... And before you bring them to me, you will go east and stand under the Split Ash, out past the pools at one-seventy, one-twelve. I want you to have seen it. That is the whole of the price.

options.text: Eight logs, and I go and look at the ninth.

text: Then you only get the wood you can buy. ... Come back when you have the time. It keeps.
Eight. And bring them here, do not bank them, I want to count them out of your hands. ... The pools are the safe way east. The Fallen Ash is the fast way and it wants Agility five in you.

Eight. Good weight, clean ends. ... And you saw it. Split top to root, and green on the west side, still. Fifty years like that. That is why the rule is eight and never the ninth: a thing can be that far gone and still be working. Take the hatchet. Iron. It will hold an edge in the deep stand.

Ten ash trees at the stand north-west of Oakwood. The canopy closes over it, so the walking is the hard part, not the cutting. The Canopy Walk goes over the top of the wet ground and wants Agility six. It saves near eighty metres. I do not use it. I am old and I like the ground.

The stags keep to the edges of the clearings. They do not come in past the standing stones at The Thicket. ... Nobody knows why and I will not be the one to find out. Trapper Mott sets his line out that way, which tells you what Mott is like.
Careful, that is a full seam allowance on the bench, which means: do not lean on it. You here for cord, hide, shafts, or advice? Three of those are free.

variants.text: There she is, the fletcher. You know what a shaft is for now, which puts you ahead of most of Oakwood. Lean on the bench if you like. You have earned it.
Four shafts, five Air Essence. Come back when you have both, not when you have one.

options.text: Four shafts and five measures of Air Essence, as asked.

requires.reason: Make the four shafts and mine the five essence first; Juno counts them in that order.
You need 4 Pine shafts. Fletch them from Pine logs at the bench on the west side of Millfield square.
You need 5 Air Essence. Mine it at the Air Essence Cache south-west of Millfield. Follow West Track, then head south.

options.text: What is an elemental orb actually doing?
What do you make out of hide?

text: Parts trades, both of them, one afternoon. Fletching first: shafts, which is a straight length of split log, which is to say, sticks, but good ones. Four Pine shafts. Then mining next: five measures of Air Essence from the southern cache. Here, take three Quartz as well; I have a drawer of them and no patience.

The fletching bench is in the workshed on the west side of Millfield square. Pine logs come out of Pine Grove, west of town along West Track. Follow West Track, then head south for the Air Essence Cache. Bring your pickaxe.

Four and five. Grain runs true on all four, which means: you did not rush them. Right. Wraps, take them, thick hide, they will not stop a bear but they will stop the cold. And a stack of Air Essence, because it powers Air spells before and after an upgrade.

options.text: So what does the orb do?

text: Essence powers a plain wand or staff directly. A boss orb wakes the matching altar at that region's Essence Cache. Once it is lit, the altar can turn either matching wooden weapon into an elemental one with a thousand charges. That weapon spends its charge first, then falls back to carried Essence. The same altar uses a hundred matching Essence to refill it.

Coarse hide off the march, thick hide off anything with a thorn in it, and fur pelt, which comes off the big ones and which I do not enjoy handling. Robes and wraps, mostly. Anything that has to bend rather than stop a blade.

Eleven traps. Eleven days. Nothing in any of them, not a hair, not a print, not so much as a disappointed look. Eleven. I counted them again this morning in case I had miscounted and there were fewer. There were not. There were eleven.

variants.text: Upside down. Eleven of them. For eleven days. My father set traps for forty years and I have been putting the open end in the ground. ... You could have not told me. I want you to know that I am aware you could have not told me.
Fen Crawlers. Fen Crawlers all along, eating the bait out from under. Well. That is a relief, in the way that a thing can be a relief and still leave you with eleven empty traps.
Twelve days, now. I have started counting the days you have been gone as well.

options.text: Do you want someone to walk the line for you?

requires.reason: Walk all four sites and clear the Fen Crawlers first.

options.text: Has it always gone like this for you?

text: Would you? Nobody ever does. Four places: Blackwater Pools. Gorge Head. The Thicket, and I am sorry about The Thicket. Gorge Ford. Look at all four. Then kill three of whatever is eating my bait, because something is.

options.text: Four sites, three of whatever it is.
I am sorry about your traps.

text: Thank you. The Thorn Maws on The Thicket are territorial, so they will not chase you far, they will simply be extremely present. Fen Crawlers sit between here and there, around one-fifty, one-twenty-eight, and they are the ones I would bet on for the bait.
Well? Do not soften it. Actually, do soften it. No. Do not. ... Do slightly soften it.

options.text: Fen Crawlers. They have been working the bait out from under the plates.
Fen Crawlers, yes. Also, Mott, all eleven traps are set upside down.

text: Fen Crawlers prying open the bait boxes. That explains the crushed boards. Here, take the trout, I smoked them myself and they are the one thing I have not got wrong.

variants.text: Upside... ah. Ah. Yes. Yes, that would do it, would it not. ... Take the trout. Take them. No, I insist, I would like you to have something so that the next eleven days are at least somebody's good week.

options.text: Has it always gone like this?

text: Once. One good week, four years ago. I caught nine in six days and I bought a coat with the money. ... Then the coat caught on a Ash and tore across the back, and I have not had a week since. I still have the coat. I keep it as a record.

speaker: Smith Corra
text: Corra. I work iron. Quarry ore, Oakwood charcoal, nothing softer. The prices are on the cart and they stay there. What do you need?

options.text: Where does the iron come from?

speaker: Smith Corra
text: Iron blades, helms, boots and gauntlets. Hard at the edge, soft at the spine, so it bends before it snaps. Ash shields for anyone who wants wood between them and the teeth. Limestone by the sack for your own furnace. Look over the cart. What you see is what it costs.

options.text: Where does the iron come from?

speaker: Smith Corra
text: The Forest Quarry. Out the Quarry Gate by the wagon, a short walk east. Five seams, all iron, good grade. Mine it, bank it on the Counting House porch, walk back. Smelt your own. You learn the metal that way.

Hillcrest. Nineteen crew, one wall, no dig. We stopped six months ago and we have eaten for six months, which is a harder trick than digging. State your business and state it in the order you intend to do it.

variants.text: Sixteen in the vault and you came over the ledge. That is on the board. Anything you want measured on this moor, I have measured it.
Ten out of the Lower Quarry, one climb, sixteen in the vault. In that order.

requires.reason: Cobalt needs Mining 10. Arden does not hand out work he knows you cannot start.
Broken Ledge needs Agility 10, and the whole point of the job is the ledge.

options.text: Sixteen Cobalt are in the vault.

requires.reason: Ten mined, the ledge climbed, then sixteen banked. Arden checks the board, not your word.

options.text: Why does the ledge matter so much to you?

text: Three things, in this order. One: ten Cobalt out of the Lower Quarry on terrace one. Two: climb Broken Ledge at least once, so you have the number in your legs and not just on a board. Three: sixteen Cobalt ore in the Hillcrest vault. Then tell me which way you walked.

Good. Figures, since you will want them. Bank to Upper Highland by road: one hundred and eighty-eight metres, three legs, two ramps. Bank to Upper Highland over the ledge: forty-six metres and a six second climb. That is the whole of the argument and it is not close.

Sixteen. Checked. And you came over the ledge, which the timings say plainly enough. Take the pickaxe, it is crew issue and it is better than anything the stall has, and take the money before the store hut hears about it.

Because the moor is vertical and everybody plans it flat. Three terraces between this counter and that seam. A crew that walks the road does four trips a shift. A crew that climbs does nine. Same ore, same arms, same day. The route is the job.

Because we hit a room. Stone Cavern mouth. Twelve metres of black in a grey face, and nineteen crew who all wanted to be somewhere else. I do not pay people to be somewhere else. Ask Watcher Hale. It is his rota.
Nine years on the blue-black. It sparks when you break it. In the dark it keeps sparking for a while after, which nobody likes talking about, so. What do you want.

variants.text: Cobalt. That is what it is, that is all it is, and I have watched a spell go into it and come back out again and I know what it is doing now. Nine years of calling it that. Ridiculous.
Storm Scarab first. Back to Farmland, west of the Air Essence Cache. Kill it without waiting for me. The Essence I gave you already lets your starter wand cast.
The Storm Scarab is dead. Good. Its Air Orb is still in the loot pile unless you picked it up, so go and pick it up.
Take the Air Orb to the ruined altar at the Air Essence Cache and wake it. Then fletch the pine into shafts and a staff, use the awakened altar to make the Air Staff, and put it in your main hand.
Now Voltrend. Get Magic to five. Use Frogs, and return to the awakened Air Altar if you somehow chew through a thousand charges.
Magic five. Six Cobalt ore. Bring it here and we find out whether I was right.

options.text: What does it do in the dark?

requires.reason: Vess wants somebody who can actually cut Cobalt. That is Mining 10.
Kill the Storm Scarab, loot its Air Orb, awaken the Air Altar, make and equip the Air Staff, and get Magic to 5 first.
You need 6 Cobalt ore in your bag.

options.text: Remind me where the Storm Scarab is.

text: It holds. Whatever you put in it, it holds it, and it gives it back later when nobody is looking. I want somebody to put something in it on purpose so I can stop imagining what it is holding. Here. Pine from my brother's stock and 100 Air Essence. The Air Orb is not mine to give. Go back to Farmland, kill the Storm Scarab west of the Air Essence Cache, and take its orb. Use it on the ruined altar at the cache, then fletch the wood into a staff and make an Air Staff at the awakened altar. Get Magic to five, and bring me six ore.

options.text: Storm Scarab, Air Orb, staff, Magic five, six ore.
I would rather not touch it.

text: No. No, that is fair. That is the reasonable position. I have not held it for nine years.

Go south through Woodlands to Millfield. Follow West Track out of town, then head south to the Air Essence Cache. The Storm Scarab roams about 42 metres west of the cache. Kill it, then loot the Air Orb from the pile it leaves. It will be there, but it will not jump into your bag. At a fletching bench, make Pine Shafts from an Pine log, then use three shafts to make an Pine Staff. Use the Air Orb on the Air Essence Altar at the cache to awaken it, then turn the Pine Staff into an Air Staff there. Equip the Air Staff. It starts with 1000 charges and spends those before carried Air Essence. The same altar fills it back to 1000 for 100 Air Essence. Then use Voltrend on Frogs at River Shallows. Do not practise on Cairn Treaders.

Go on. ... There. It took it. It took the whole cast and the fracture line went white and then it just, sat there, being a rock. Nine years. It is a rock that likes magic. That is all it ever was. Take the essence. Keep the staff you made; I never liked what the wood reminded me of.

options.text: Then who is stacking the cairns?

text: Five in the Lower Quarry, terrace one, next to the hole. Three at Upper Highland, terrace four, and that one runs dry if you are any good. Take the ledge up, do not take the road, the road is for carts and regret.
Not us. Ask Cairnkeeper Ode. She knows every stone up there by name and she has gone quiet about it, which is the part that bothers me. Cairnkeeper going quiet. That is a weather sign, that is.

You will forgive me. I am counting. There are four hundred and eleven cairns on this moor and it is my office to know the shape of each one. Nineteen of them are the wrong shape this season, and I did not put a hand to any of them.

variants.text: The hall is kept. The stone is laid and the line is closed, and the gate beyond it is open, which is a thing I did and not a thing that happened to me. Ask me anything now. I have no more silence to spend.
You are in the middle of an office. Tell me where you have got to.

requires.reason: Ode will not send anyone under Melee 10 up the terraces. Cairn Treaders hold the ground at (100, -110).
Mining 10, because the line ends in a quarry and she will not lead you somewhere you cannot work.

options.text: The Great Cairn has been re-stacked.

requires.reason: Go and see the Great Cairn on terrace four first. Take the Second Ramp, then the Third Ramp, and head west.

options.text: There is a stone door in the second chamber with three levers on it.

requires.reason: Clear the Lit Gallery and reach The Collapse first; she will not describe a door you have not found.

options.text: The door is open. Give me the keeping-stone.

requires.reason: The Three-Lever Door has to be open before she will part with the stone.

options.text: I no longer have the keeping-stone.

requires.reason: Ode has cut you three keeping-stones already. She will not cut a fourth, and she is right not to.

options.text: What is under the Great Cairn?

requires.reason: Ode will answer that when the Long Cairn is finished and not one hour before.

text: The Great Cairn on terrace four. It was head height and forty paces round when the quarry opened and it is neither of those things now. Go and stand at it and look at the top three courses, then come back and tell me I am not an old woman miscounting stones.
Bank, Second Ramp, Third Ramp, then west. Cairn Treaders hold the middle ground at about one hundred, minus one hundred and ten, and they do not leash early. Go fed.

Re-stacked. Not fallen, not robbed. Re-stacked, by something with a sense of order and more patience than the living have. ... The nineteen make a line. It runs off terrace four, down both ramps and into the quarry face, and it ends at a hole my neighbours have a rota for. Go and ask Watcher Hale what his rota has actually seen. He will tell you if you ask him plainly.

speaker: Cairnkeeper Ode
text:
I know that door. The masons cut it and the masons left a rule with it, and I have the rule by heart because it is the sort of thing my office is for.

Three levers, side by side, and a mark cut in the lintel above each one. A WEDGE, which is the mason's mark for stone. A DROP, which is their mark for water. And a CLOSED EYE, which is their mark for the dark. The marks are the only labels; the levers themselves are identical.

The rule they left is one line: THE MOOR GIVES STONE, THEN WATER, THEN DARK. That is the order they meant, and that is the order the door wants, and it is the order in which this whole moor was made, if you have ever looked at a terrace face. Pull them wrong and nothing happens except that you have been wrong.

So. Tell me the order and I will tell you whether you have it.

options.text: Wedge, then drop, then closed eye.
Wedge, then closed eye, then drop.
Drop, then wedge, then closed eye.
Drop, then closed eye, then wedge.
Closed eye, then wedge, then drop.
Closed eye, then drop, then wedge.
Ode. Just tell me which order.

text: No. Think about the line again: the moor gives stone, then water, then dark. Stone is the wedge. Water is the drop. The dark is the closed eye. It is not a riddle, it is a rota, and rotas are written in the order they are worked.

Wedge, drop, closed eye. Stone, water, dark. That is the door's own order and it will answer to it now. Go down to The Collapse, the second chamber of Stone Cavern, and open the stone door. It will not argue with you twice.
Wedge, drop, closed eye. There. It costs me nothing to say it and it is costing you daylight not to know it. The stone door is in The Collapse, the second chamber of Stone Cavern. Open it.

Then the hall is reachable and the office can be finished properly. This is a keeping-stone. Garnet, cut and not polished, and it goes on the top course of the cairn in that hall. Two Vault Custodians stand over it and they will have to be moved, and I am sorry, and I mean it. Do not sell the stone on the way.

Then here is another, and I will not ask. Garnet is common on this moor and patience is not, so I have a great deal of one and I am spending the other. Top course of the cairn in the Cairn Hall, the third chamber of Stone Cavern. That is where this garnet belongs.

options.text: It will get there this time.

text: A cairn is a promise that somebody was here and somebody else noticed. That is all. It is not magic and it is not a grave marker, whatever the quarry crew tell each other. It is a count kept in stone by people who could not write.

Stone. Only stone, all the way down, and I have known that for thirty years. The thing that has been re-stacking them is not looking for what is underneath. It is keeping the count. Somebody taught it to keep the count, and then that somebody stopped coming, and it has been doing the office alone ever since. ... Yes. I have thought about that a great deal.
Afternoon. I am on the mouth until six. It is fine. It is mostly fine. It is a hole and I look at it, and then somebody else looks at it, and that is the rota.

variants.text: You went in. ... You went in, and you came back out, and I have been on this rota for six months. I am not sure how I feel about that. Mostly relieved. Mostly.

options.text: Tell me plainly what comes out of Stone Cavern.

requires.reason: Hale will not talk about the mouth until Cairnkeeper Ode has sent you. Speak to her first.

options.text: What does the mouth look like from here?

text:
Plainly. Right. ... Four Blind Cave Weavers in the first chamber, the lit one. Somebody keeps those torches burning, and it is not us, and I would rather they went out. Past that there is a collapse, and it is dark, and more weavers move through the fallen beams. And there is a door with three levers that none of us could work out, and after that... I have not been after that. Nobody on the rota has been after that.

Stone Cavern mouth is on terrace one, next to the quarry. It opens into The Lit Gallery. Go armed. Please go armed.

options.text: What does it look like from here?

text: Nineteen of us, so a shift every nineteen days, which is reasonable. It has been my shift eleven times since the spring. I have not raised it. People swap for reasons and I do not like to ask what the reasons are.

Twelve metres of black in a grey face. You can see it from anywhere on terrace one, which is the trouble, really. It is not that it is frightening to look at. It is that you can always look at it, from anywhere, and so you do.

speaker: Master Garek
text: Master Garek. I teach new hunters to read a contract before they take one. Small targets still punish carelessness. What do you need?

options.text: How do I take a hunt?
Where should a new hunter begin?

speaker: Master Garek
text: Open the Journal and choose Hunts. Refresh the board if it has no offers, then accept one. You can carry one active hunt. It tracks your credited kills in the named region; once the count is met, claim the reward on that same tab. The board only offers enemies you can currently reach.

speaker: Master Garek
text: Take a target close to your own level and stay where you have an open way out. If you cannot find a suitable offer, improve your combat skill or open another route before you try again. Returning alive is part of the lesson.

options.text: How do I take a hunt?
I will keep that in mind.

speaker: Master Vardan
text: Master Vardan. The wilderness does not care what you meant to fight. The Hunts board can offer a wilderness target once it considers you ready and the route reachable. I do not promise what the board has not shown you.

options.text: How do I check for a wilderness hunt?
What should I expect at the Black Keep?

speaker: Master Vardan
text: Open Journal, then Hunts, and refresh the offers. A wilderness contract appears only when its targets are registered, reachable, and within the board's combat range. Take one contract at a time. Read the region and target names before you accept; the keep is no place to discover you prepared for the wrong enemy.

speaker: Master Vardan
text: The Black Keep has an approach, a gate, and a court. The dead hold the walls and the court. Use the named route in the Locations journal, check your food and equipment before the gate, and do not cross the threshold just because the first guard fell.

options.text: How do I check for a wilderness hunt?

speaker: Master Aevra
text: I am Aevra, trail reader for the gardens. Some lights are travelers, some blossoms are watching you, and a quiet path may only be quiet for a moment. What would you like to know?

options.text: What should I watch for in the gardens?
Can I take a fairy hunt contract?

speaker: Master Aevra
text: Lantern sprites drift along the lit paths. Moonpetal stalkers defend their beds, and the deeper dewglass weavers keep to the shaded trellises. Watch a creature before you approach it. A forager may ignore you; the one guarding a bloom may not.

options.text: Can I take a fairy hunt contract?
I will observe before I move.

speaker: Master Aevra
text: Not for the fairy lands yet. The current Hunts board covers reachable targets in the mainland regions; it does not issue contracts for Faeholme or Gloamgarden. You can still inspect a local creature and learn its habits, but I will not pretend there is a contract when there is none.

options.text: Tell me about the local trails.

speaker: Morrow
text: The gate is open. Keep your eyes on the road beyond it. What are you looking for?

speaker: Morrow
text: Three stalls face the square: potions to the west, arms in the middle, and cosmic goods to the east. The bank is farther west.

speaker: Morrow
text: Take the road north past the foundry turn, then follow the lamps toward Starhaven. Do not mistake a light off the road for a guide.

speaker: Vell
text: I keep the ledgers here. Their ink has outlasted more than one keeper.

speaker: Vell
text: The bank counter is west of the square, beneath the short porch. Bring your goods to the counter.

speaker: Vell
text: The market stalls are just east of here. The apothecary has potions; the arms and cosmic stalls keep the rest.

speaker: Ossin
text: The bottles are sorted by strength. Read the label before you drink.

speaker: Ossin
text: Lastlight stocks melee, magic and defence potions through rank three. Rank three begins at tier fifty; earlier ranks are still on the shelf.

speaker: Ossin
text: Each potion lasts five minutes. A stronger one replaces a weaker effect of the same kind; they do not add together.

speaker: Edda
text: A sound edge and a sound clasp will take you farther than a grand name.

speaker: Edda
text: The arms stall has ordinary cindersteel weapons and a complete armour set, along with a teak shield. The forge stands just east of the square.

speaker: Edda
text: The potion stall is west of the arms. The cosmic stall is east. All three face the square.

speaker: Neris
text: The lamps show the path. They cannot make it harmless.

options.text: What does the cosmic stall carry?

speaker: Neris
text: Look for wands, staves, robes and runes at the east stall. The trader keeps practical tools there, not prophecies.

speaker: Neris
text: Starhaven stands beyond the foundry road. Its lamps burn colder, but someone still tends every one.

speaker: Tarn
text: You reached the gate. That is reason enough to stop and check your gear.

speaker: Tarn
text: The three stalls stand north of the square. Potions are west, arms in the centre, and cosmic goods east. The bank is down the west walk.

speaker: Tarn
text: The south gate returns to the foundry road. Keep to its lamps until the Lastlight track comes into view.

speaker: Maer
text: The ledger is open. I can still read every hand that wrote in it.

speaker: Maer
text: Follow the west walk to the bank porch. The counter is inside the northern end of the yard.

speaker: Maer
text: Return to the square and look north. The potion, arms and cosmic stalls face the same lane.

speaker: Sable
text: The glass is old. The measures are exact.

speaker: Sable
text: Starhaven stocks rank-four melee, magic and defence potions at tier seventy. Ranks one through three remain available here.

speaker: Sable
text: Choose the effect you need before a hard fight. It lasts five minutes; another potion of the same kind replaces it rather than stacking.

speaker: Orun
text: Nightglass takes patience. It has no use for speeches.

options.text: What do you keep in stock?

speaker: Orun
text: The arms stall has an ordinary nightglass sword, shield and full armour set, plus gathering tools. Each piece is made for long use.

speaker: Orun
text: Potions stand west of my counter. Cosmic goods are east. The bank is across the square and down the west walk.

speaker: Hush
text: You may stand under this roof until you know your next step.

options.text: Where can I find the bank?

speaker: Hush
text: Take the west walk from the square. Maer keeps the bank counter beneath the porch.

speaker: Hush
text: The road still needs a place to pause. We mend the gates, keep the lamps lit and send travellers onward with what they need.
